items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A causal law \(P\) is a Borel probability measure on \([0,1]\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}^2\times\{0,1\}\) for \((X,A,Y^{\mathrm{pot}},Y)\), with observed marginal \(P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) on \(\mathcal O=[0,1]\times\{0,1\}^2\), selected versions \(f_P,e_P,\mu_{0,P},\mu_{1,P}\), contrast \(\tau_P=\mu_{1,P}-\mu_{0,P}\) and target \(\theta(P)=\tau_P(1/2)\); the class \(\mathcal P\) is the complete model with radius \(L=3\), and a dataset \(D\in\mathcal O^n\), \(n\ge2\), is drawn from \((P^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\).

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: Pure \(\epsilon\)-differentially-private release under replacement adjacency: a mechanism is an everywhere-defined Markov kernel \(M:\mathcal O^n\rightsquigarrow\mathcal B\) into a standard Borel space, datasets at Hamming distance one satisfy \(M(D,E)\le e^{\epsilon}M(D',E)\), \(\epsilon\in(0,1]\); scalar releases take \(\mathcal B=\mathbb R\), interval releases take \(\mathcal B=\mathcal I\) (connected Borel subsets of \(\mathbb R\) coded by endpoints and inclusion flags); risks and coverages integrate both the data law and the mechanism, and laws of outputs are compared in total variation and datasets in expected Hamming transport \(W_{\mathrm H}\).

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl: Public tuning and the density-free private ratio: public radius \(h\in(0,1/4]\), cell count \(k\ge2\), width \(\delta=2h/k\), equal cells \((C_j)\) of \([x_0-h,x_0+h]\), count-weighted pair statistics \(S_N,S_D\) built from kernels \(K_N,K_D\), population occupancy weights and conditional pair moments, public envelopes \(\mathcal A,d_0,b,V(h,\delta)\), independent Laplace noise of scale \(12/\epsilon\), the floored clipped ratio \(\widehat T_{h,k}\), the interval \(\widehat I_{h,k}\), the benchmark scale \(r(n,\epsilon)\), and the publicly tuned outputs \(\widehat T^*,\widehat I^*=I^*_{n,\epsilon}\) with interval-question outputs \(\ell,c_I,C_I\).

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: Lower-bound experiments inside \(\mathcal P\): macro radius \(h_{\mathrm L}\in(0,1/4]\), micro radius \(\delta_{\mathrm L}=h_{\mathrm L}^5\), amplitude \(\kappa=2^{-12}\), separation \(t=\kappa h_{\mathrm L}\), envelope \(g\), bump \(q=g^2\), overlapping cosine frame \(\phi_j\) on the finite index set \(\mathcal J\), uniform signs \(\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^{\mathcal J}\), perturbation \(S_\lambda\), the fair null \(P_0\), sign alternatives \(P_\lambda\) and their dataset mixture \(Q_n\), direct alternative \(P_1\), Fourier marks \(U=2A-1,V_Y=2Y-1\) with conditional likelihood \(L_\lambda\), and, given covariates, the shared-sign graph \(G_X\), its components \(C\) of size \(m\), component mark laws \(P_{0,C},Q_C\) with mass arrays \(a,b,c\), overlap \(\alpha\), and common-mass coupling \(\Gamma_C\).

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl:
The class consists of causal laws on the stated binary-record experiment:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal P=\bigl\{P\in\operatorname{Prob}([0,1]\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}^2\times\{0,1\}):{}&
P\{Y=Y(A)\}=1,\\
&Y^{\mathrm{pot}}\perp\!\!\!\perp A\mid X\ [P],\\
&P_X\ll dx,\quad 1/2\le f_P\le3/2\quad(dx\text{-a.e.}),\\
&1/4\le e_P(x)\le3/4\quad\text{for every }x\in[0,1],\\
&|e_P(x)-e_P(x')|\le L|x-x'|^{1/10}\quad\text{for every }x,x'\in[0,1],\\
&|\mu_{0,P}(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x')|\le L|x-x'|^{1/10}\quad\text{for every }x,x'\in[0,1],\\
&|\tau_P(x)-\tau_P(x')|\le L|x-x'|\quad\text{for every }x,x'\in[0,1]\bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The displayed function conditions concern the selected versions of the observational regressions. The density is unknown and only measurable. There are no fixed interior restrictions on either arm mean. This definition imposes only properties of a member law, with no estimator, tuning, or inference conditions.

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl: \(\mathfrak M_{n,\epsilon}(\mathcal B)=\{M:\mathcal O^n\rightsquigarrow\mathcal B:\forall D,D^{\prime}\in\mathcal O^n,\ d_{\mathrm H}(D,D^{\prime})=1\Rightarrow\forall E\in\mathcal B(\mathcal B),\ M(D,E)\le\exp(\epsilon)M(D^{\prime},E)\}\).

items.label: Definition P-4
items.nl: \(H_{n,\epsilon}=\inf\{\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}E_{(P^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},I}\operatorname{Leb}(I(D)):I\in\mathfrak M_{n,\epsilon}(\mathcal I),\ \inf_{P\in\mathcal P}\Pr_{(P^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},I}\{\theta(P)\in I(D)\}\ge9/10\}\).

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl:
For each occupied public cell, let \(s\) be its record count and let the sums below run over its records. If \(s<2\), both contributions are zero. If \(s\ge2\), the numerator and denominator contributions are respectively
\[
\frac{2\{s\sum AY-(\sum A)(\sum Y)\}}{s-1},\qquad
\frac{2\{s\sum A-(\sum A)^2\}}{s-1}.
\]
Sum these contributions to obtain \(S_N(D)\) and \(S_D(D)\). Draw the independent noises \(\xi_N,\xi_D\) of scale \(12/\epsilon\) once, and release
\[
\widetilde S=(S_N+\xi_N,S_D+\xi_D).
\]
Postprocess this one release into
\[
\widehat T_{h,k}=\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}
\left\{\frac{S_N+\xi_N}{\max\{d_0,S_D+\xi_D\}}\right\},
\]
\[
\widehat I_{h,k}=\left[
\max\{-1,\widehat T_{h,k}-\sqrt{10V(h,\delta)}\},
\min\{1,\widehat T_{h,k}+\sqrt{10V(h,\delta)}\}
\right].
\]
All parameters are public, \(d_0=3\mathcal A/64>0\), and \(\delta=2h/k\). Counts and moment sums need only be computed for occupied cells; the map is defined on every \(D\in\mathcal O^n\).

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl:
If \(r(n,\epsilon)\ge1/8\), set \(\widehat T^*=0\) and \(\widehat I^*=[-1,1]\). Otherwise set
\[
h=2^{-\lceil\log_2(1/r(n,\epsilon))\rceil},\qquad
k=2h^{-4},\qquad \delta=2h/k=h^5,
\]
and return \((\widehat T^*,\widehat I^*)=(\widehat T_{h,k},\widehat I_{h,k})\) using \texttt{def:private-ratio}. This is a single sample map with public tuning depending only on \(n,\epsilon\).

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl: For each \(\lambda\), take \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), \(A\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}((1+\sqrt tS_\lambda(x))/2)\), and conditionally independent binary potential outcomes, independent of \(A\) given \(X\), with means \((1-\sqrt tS_\lambda(x)-tq(x))/2\) and \((1-\sqrt tS_\lambda(x)+tq(x))/2\) for control and treatment respectively. Set \(Y=Y(A)\); the resulting causal law is \(P_\lambda\). Average its observed product law over uniform \(\lambda\) to form \(Q_n\).

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl: For \(z,w\in\{0,1\}^{2m}\), set \(\Gamma_C(z,w)=c_z\mathbf1\{z=w\}+(a_z-c_z)(b_w-c_w)/(1-\alpha)\) when \(\alpha<1\), and \(\Gamma_C(z,w)=c_z\mathbf1\{z=w\}\) when \(\alpha=1\). Use the same covariates and the product of these kernels across lexicographically selected graph components.

items.label: Definition P-9
items.nl: Under \(P_1\), draw \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\); conditional on \(X\), draw \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), \(Y(0)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), and \(Y(1)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2+tq(X))\) independently; set \(Y=Y(A)\).

items.label: Definition P-10
items.nl:
Define \(I^*_{n,\epsilon}=\widehat I^*\) by the following explicit inversion. If \(r(n,\epsilon)\ge1/8\), accept every \(\vartheta\in[-1,1]\) and return \([-1,1]\). Otherwise use the public \(h,k,\delta\) in \texttt{def:public-tuning}, compute the single release \(\widetilde S\) in \texttt{def:private-ratio}, and put
\[
B_D=\max\{d_0,\widetilde S_D\},\qquad
B_N=\operatorname{clip}_{[-B_D,B_D]}(\widetilde S_N),\qquad
\rho=\sqrt{10V(h,\delta)}.
\]
Accept a candidate \(\vartheta\in[-1,1]\) precisely when
\[
|B_N-\vartheta B_D|\le\rho B_D.
\]
Return the interval hull of the accepted set; if that set were empty, return \([-1,1]\). The public radius retains the bias envelope \(b\), occupancy scale \(\mathcal A\), and Laplace second moment through \(V(h,\delta)\).

items.label: Assumption A-9
items.nl: \(\forall D,D^{\prime}\in\mathcal O^n\text{ with }d_{\mathrm H}(D,D^{\prime})=1,\quad\forall E\in\mathcal B(\mathcal B),\quad M(D,E)\le \exp(\epsilon) M(D^{\prime},E)\).

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: For every \(P\in\mathcal P\), the observed-law contrast has a unique continuous representative \(\tau_P\), \(\theta(P)\in[-1,1]\), and \(\tau_P(X)=E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X]\) almost surely. Its value at \(x_0\) is identified from \(P^{\mathrm{obs}}\).

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl: For every \(P\in\mathcal P\) and every public \(h,k\), \(\overline N=\sum_{j=1}^k w_j\nu_j\), \(\overline D=\sum_{j=1}^k w_jd_j\), \(d_j\ge3/8\), and \(|\nu_j-\theta(P)d_j|\le b d_j\). Moreover \(\mathcal A/8\le W(P)\le9\mathcal A/2\), \(\overline D\ge d_0\), and \(|\overline N/\overline D-\theta(P)|\le b\).

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl: For every pair \(D,D^{\prime}\in\mathcal O^n\) with \(d_{\mathrm H}(D,D^{\prime})=1\), \(\|(S_N(D),S_D(D))-(S_N(D^{\prime}),S_D(D^{\prime}))\|_1\le12\). For iid data from every \(P\in\mathcal P\), \(\max\{\operatorname{Var}(S_N),\operatorname{Var}(S_D)\}\le18W(P)\). These claims include occupancies zero, one, and two and input datasets outside the model.

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl: For every \(h_{\mathrm L}\in(0,1/4]\), \(P_0\in\mathcal P\) and \(P_\lambda\in\mathcal P\) for every \(\lambda\), with \(\theta(P_0)=0\) and \(\theta(P_\lambda)=t\). The likelihood is \(L_\lambda(x,U,V_Y)=1+U\sqrt tS_\lambda+V_Y\sqrt t(tq-1)S_\lambda+UV_Yt(q-S_\lambda^2)\); \(E_\lambda P_\lambda^{\mathrm{obs}}=P_0^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(\chi^2(Q_n,(P_0^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n})\le\exp(160n^2t^2h_{\mathrm L}\delta_{\mathrm L})-1\).

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl: Given any covariate vector, the conditional laws under \(Q_n\) and \((P_0^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\) factor over components of \(G_X\); singleton laws coincide. For every component \(C\), \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q_C,P_{0,C})\le4tm^2\). The product of \(\Gamma_C\) is a Borel coupling with the two required dataset marginals. If \(n\delta_{\mathrm L}\le1/128\), then \(W_{\mathrm H}(Q_n,(P_0^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n})\le1024tn^2h_{\mathrm L}\delta_{\mathrm L}\). Under the same condition \(n\delta_{\mathrm L}\le1/128\), for every standard Borel \(\mathcal B\) and \(M\in\mathfrak M_{n,\epsilon}(\mathcal B)\), \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(MQ_n,M(P_0^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n})\le2048\epsilon tn^2h_{\mathrm L}\delta_{\mathrm L}\).

items.label: Lemma L-6
items.nl:
For dataset laws \(Q,Q'\) on \(\mathcal O^n\), every \(M\in\mathfrak M_{n,\epsilon}(\mathcal B)\) satisfies
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(MQ,MQ')\le2\epsilon W_{\mathrm H}(Q,Q').
\]
Every Markov kernel, regardless of privacy, also satisfies \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(MQ,MQ')\le d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q,Q')\). If \(Q\ll Q'\) and its chi-square divergence is finite, then
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q,Q')\le\tfrac12\sqrt{\chi^2(Q,Q')}.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-7
items.nl:
For every \(n\ge2\) and \(0<\epsilon\le1\), there exist two finite mixtures of observed product laws of members of \(\mathcal P\), denoted \(Q^{(0)},Q^{(1)}\), and a number \(\Delta\ge2^{-14}r(n,\epsilon)\). Every member of the first mixture has \(\theta(P)=0\), and every member of the second has \(\theta(P)=\Delta\). For every standard Borel output space \(\mathcal B\) and every \(M\in\mathfrak M_{n,\epsilon}(\mathcal B)\),
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(MQ^{(0)},MQ^{(1)})\le1/4.
\]
The mixtures are obtained by the explicit sign or direct families with macro radii specified in the proof.

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: For every public \(h,k,n,\epsilon\), the construction \((\widehat T_{h,k},\widehat I_{h,k})\) is total and is the explicit Markov kernel defined above, built from exact-real arithmetic, cell and endpoint comparisons, and independent Laplace noise. No claim of computability on represented reals is made. This kernel is pure \(\epsilon\)-private on all of \(\mathcal O^n\). Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P\), \(E(\widehat T_{h,k}-\theta(P))^2\le V(h,\delta)\), \(\Pr\{\theta(P)\in\widehat I_{h,k}\}\ge9/10\), and \(E\operatorname{Leb}(\widehat I_{h,k})\le\min\{2,2\sqrt{10V(h,\delta)}\}\). The publicly tuned outputs satisfy \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}E|\widehat T^*-\theta(P)|\le2^{18}r(n,\epsilon)\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}E\operatorname{Leb}(\widehat I^*)\le2^{22}r(n,\epsilon)\), with coverage at least \(9/10\) at every law.

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl: For every \(n\ge2\) and \(0<\epsilon\le1\), \(2^{-20}r(n,\epsilon)\le R_{n,\epsilon}\le2^{18}r(n,\epsilon)\). The lower bound ranges over every total randomized pure-private scalar mechanism in the same observation experiment. The upper bound is attained by \(\widehat T^*\) on the entire class \(\mathcal P\), including every admissible unknown measurable \(f_P\).

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl: The scale \(r(n,\epsilon)\) equals \(n^{-1/4}\) when \(\epsilon\ge n^{-1/4}\), \((n^2\epsilon)^{-1/7}\) when \(n^{-3/5}\le\epsilon\le n^{-1/4}\), \((n\epsilon)^{-1/2}\) when \(n^{-1}\le\epsilon\le n^{-3/5}\), and \(1\) when \(0<\epsilon\le n^{-1}\). In particular, at \(\epsilon=1\) the scale identity is \(r(n,1)=n^{-1/4}\); calling this the nonprivate order is descriptive and does not assert an unrestricted minimax-risk bound. For every budget sequence in \((0,1]\), \(R_{n,\epsilon}\to0\) if and only if \(n\epsilon\to\infty\).

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
The answer to Open-ended Question 1 is
\[
\ell(n,\epsilon)=r(n,\epsilon),\qquad c_I=2^{-20},\qquad C_I=2^{22},\qquad
I^*_{n,\epsilon}=\widehat I^*.
\]
Here \(\widehat I^*\) is the explicit total publicly tuned connected-interval kernel in \texttt{def:public-tuning}: it returns \([-1,1]\) for \(r\ge1/8\), and otherwise returns the interval in the single-release construction \texttt{def:private-ratio}, with its specified dyadic \(h\), integer \(k=2h^{-4}\), \(\delta=h^5\), and public radius \(\sqrt{10V(h,\delta)}\). For every \(n\ge2\) and \(0<\epsilon\le1\),
\[
2^{-20}r(n,\epsilon)\le H_{n,\epsilon}
\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}E\operatorname{Leb}(I^*_{n,\epsilon}(D))
\le2^{22}r(n,\epsilon),
\qquad
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}\Pr\{\theta(P)\in I^*_{n,\epsilon}(D)\}\ge9/10.
\]
The converse ranges over all total randomized private connected-interval kernels with the stated class-wide coverage. In conjunction with the scalar frontier,
\[
2^{-38}R_{n,\epsilon}\le H_{n,\epsilon}\le2^{42}R_{n,\epsilon}.
\]
Thus the risk and honest expected-length scales are uniformly equivalent; interval optimality follows from the interval-specific simultaneous-containment argument in the proof.

items.label: Cited result lem:efron-stein-replacement
items.nl: For independent random elements \(B_1,\ldots,B_s\) and a square-integrable measurable statistic \(Z=\Psi(B_1,\ldots,B_s)\), let \(Z^{(i)}\) replace \(B_i\) by an independent copy. Then \[\operatorname{Var}(Z)\le\frac12\sum_{i=1}^s E\{(Z-Z^{(i)})^2\}.\]

items.label: Cited result lem:bounded-differences-mgf
items.nl: Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_s\) be independent random elements. Let the bounded measurable function \(\Psi\) change by at most \(c_i\ge0\) when only its \(i\)-th argument changes. For every \(u\ge0\), \[E\exp\{u(\Psi-E\Psi)\}\le\exp\left\{\frac{u^2}{8}\sum_{i=1}^s c_i^2\right\}.\]

items.label: Cited result lem:cayley-labeled-tree-count
items.nl: For an integer \(s\ge2\), there are exactly \(s^{s-2}\) undirected trees on a specified set of \(s\) distinct vertex labels.
